[Discussion] What's your favorite video game protagonist with a personality?

Kain from Legacy of Kain. The whole series is basically understanding his decision to rule a ruined world rather than die to preserve it. Initially, it's just the "evil" choice at the end of a game, and from there on out it turns into different shades of grey as you learn more about his character. You see him from the eyes of another character, and he seems in control, cool, almost omnipotent, and unpredictable. As you chase him, he subtly reveals doubts, regrets, hopes, uncertainty, and you end up realizing the two characters share two parts of the truth that you've known as the player all along, having been able to play as both characters.

I really like his character progression, because it's like he's removing a series of masks. First that he didn't care for the world he doomed. Then that he was all powerful, and in control. Then finally, even though throughout the series he's been spoken of as (and even speaks about himself this way) inhuman, you see that he has hopes for the future, and a subtle hint that he had not felt as confident in his actions as he seemed, and had even been afraid of being wrong. He was very masterfully written, which is no surprise, because Amy Hennig took over writing (then directing) for the series after the first game, Blood Omen.
Borderlands Pre-Sequel spoiler: counts, I'd go with him. A complex and humorous character and shows that the conflict between the characters isn't black and white.

Geralt, from The Witcher series. He's a mutant, as reviled as the monsters he hunts. But the people, kings and peasants alike, rely on him to hunt monsters and break curses, and they hate him for it. However, these data and others showing a correlation between high disease incidence and high socio-economic level do not prove a causal link between infections and immune disorders. Proof of principle of the hygiene hypothesis is brought by animal models and to a lesser degree by intervention trials in humans. Underlying mechanisms are multiple and complex. They include decreased consumption of homeostatic factors and immunoregulation, involving various regulatory T cell subsets and Toll-like receptor stimulation. These mechanisms could originate, to some extent, from changes in microbiota caused by changes in lifestyle, particularly in inflammatory bowel diseases. Taken together, these data open new therapeutic perspectives in the prevention of autoimmune and allergic diseases.
